title: The EC armor shape backtracks catastrophically on header lines with trailing spaces, so a planted text holds the leak scan and publish for minutes
goal: kbcommon.SECRETS' EC alternative runs in linear time: a failing input of many header lines with trailing spaces or literal escapes is scanned in well under a second, while every key form BG-3vnu37rq flags still flags

run:
import base64, os, sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbcommon
d = "-" * 5
arm = d + "BEGIN EC PRIVATE KEY" + d
b = base64.b64encode(os.urandom(96)).decode()
hit = lambda t: any(k == "secret" for k, _ in kbcommon.leak_hits(t))
t = time.monotonic(); hit(arm + "\nA: b \n" * 22 + "!"); s = time.monotonic() - t
print("22 trailing-space headers took %.2f s" % s)
sys.exit(0 if s < 0.2 else 1)

notes: Found by the SP-tsb23kev focused review of BG-3vnu37rq (reviewer session a419aba4) on origin/main 902e961a9; repro fails there.
